narrative_purpose: Shows the prolemuris forelimb that splits at the elbow into two forearms - the living clue, read as one limb-tip dividing in two rather than two limbs fusing into one.
subject: A close anatomical study of a single prolemuris forelimb against a dark canopy backdrop: one slender upper arm extends from the shoulder to the elbow, where it cleanly divides into two complete separate forearms, each with its own wrist and slender clawed hand. The single shared humerus and the two distinct forearm bones are subtly visible beneath translucent skin.

style: Painterly naturalist specimen study, hand-painted texture, anatomical intimacy.
detail_level: Crisp on the elbow split, the shared upper arm, and the two forearms and hands; canopy background dissolving into haze.
